lead: Hair perfume or hair mist is a light fragrance spray made for the hair, as an alternative to applying perfume to skin. People use it to leave a pleasant scent trail that moves with the hair, so they smell good as they walk past, and to refresh scent between washes.

Sellers describe hair mists as lighter and gentler than skin perfume: one brand article says perfumes are formulated with high alcohol concentrations meant for skin, and that hair mists use a lighter base with conditioning ingredients such as panthenol and betaine.[2] The same article says hair fibres hold fragrance molecules longer than skin because hair lacks the warmth and oils that break scent down, and suggests pairing a hair mist with a perfume on pulse points. It is published by a company that sells hair mists and cites no independent research.[2]

Perfume references classify light 'mists' and splashes as low-concentration products (eau fraiche, 3% or less aromatic compounds),[1] and note that perfume materials can include allergenic compounds.[1] No studies of hair-specific fragrances were found.

angle.text: People use hair mist to add scent to their hair without putting full-strength perfume on it, so their hair smells fresh and leaves a lasting impression.

infobox: Typically light; mists classed as 3% or less aromatic compounds (eau fraiche)[1]

paras: Hair mists are marketed as lighter and gentler than skin perfume, a claim made by sellers; traditional perfume application targets warm pulse points to release the scent.[1][2] Brand guidance describes spraying from a distance onto mid-lengths and ends and avoiding the scalp.[2]

Brand and beauty-press articles say the alcohol in skin perfume can dry hair with repeated use, leading to frizz or breakage, and recommend hair-specific products.[2] These statements come from sellers and lifestyle outlets rather than published trials.
Perfume materials, natural and synthetic, can include allergenic compounds.[1] Products sprayed near the scalp contact skin as well as hair.

lore.intro: Hair mists are discussed as a subtle scent layer, often combined with a skin fragrance.[2]

claims.claim: Hair holds scent longer than skin and leaves a trail as you move
claims.believers: A seller article states hair fibres hold fragrance longer than skin and recommends layering a hair mist with perfume.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies were found on scent retention in hair; the source for this claim is a company that sells hair mists.

claims.claim: Skin perfume dries out hair, so a dedicated hair mist is gentler
claims.believers: The same brand says alcohol-heavy perfume can cause frizz and breakage over time.[2]
claims.experts: Perfume references describe low-concentration mists as a distinct product class;[1] no study compared hair mist with perfume on hair.

card.summary: Light fragrance spray for hair; a niche scent layer with no studies behind it.

quick.overview:
Hair perfume is a light spray designed for hair rather than skin.

It is used to carry scent when you move.
quick.mechanism: Fragrance is deposited on hair, which is said to hold and release scent.
quick.risks: Allergen exposure from fragrance ingredients; no hair-specific studies were found.
